_note: INVENTED EXAMPLE. Sam is a made-up bookkeeper. Every name, number and result in this file is invented to show the format. Copy the shape, not the content.

slides.title: cash flow checks a small business can run
slides.kicker: Ten minutes each. No new software to buy.

slides.title: The Monday balance
slides.does: Write the bank balance on one line every Monday morning, before any email gets opened.
slides.got: Twelve Mondays in, the line shows a slide weeks before the overdraft does.

slides.title: The invoice age list
slides.does: Sort unpaid invoices by days outstanding. Anything past 30 days gets a phone call, never another email.
slides.got: Late payers answer a phone. The average wait fell from 41 days to 19.

slides.title: The tax pot
slides.does: A separate account takes 25% of every payment the day it lands, so the tax bill is already sitting there.
slides.got: The tax bill stops being a shock. The money is set aside before anyone can spend it.

slides.title: The 13-week forecast
slides.does: Thirteen rows, one per week: money expected in, money going out, and the gap between them.
slides.got: One client spotted a payroll gap nine weeks early and moved a supplier payment.

slides.title: The subscription sweep
slides.does: Once a quarter, print the card statement and circle every repeating charge nobody can name.
slides.got: Most owners find three or four forgotten tools. Cancelling them paid for the bookkeeping.

slides.title: Keep this for the next quiet Monday.

INVENTED EXAMPLE CAPTION. Most small businesses that run out of cash were profitable on paper.

Five checks, ten minutes each, none of them need new software.
